title: Reconstruction Remembered
objective: After this level you can explain how historians' verdict on Reconstruction changed from the Dunning School to W. E. B. Du Bois and later scholars.
summary: The Dunning School called Reconstruction a mistake. Du Bois’s Black Reconstruction (1935) showed freedpeople shaping it, and revisionists overturned the old verdict.

cards.headline: For decades, many Americans learned that Reconstruction was a tragic mistake.
cards.body: Then historians went back to the evidence and the verdict flipped. How does a whole era get rewritten?

cards.headline: The Dunning School
cards.body: William Archibald Dunning, a Columbia University historian, shaped how Americans understood Reconstruction, through his writings and the many historians he trained. His school called it a mistake. Ill-prepared Black officeholders, it claimed, together with Southern white “scalawags” and Northern “carpetbaggers,” brought havoc on the South.

cards.headline: Du Bois answers
cards.body: In 1935 W. E. B. Du Bois published Black Reconstruction. He showed that freedpeople were not a problem to be managed but actors who shaped Reconstruction’s politics and its gains in civil rights and democracy. Remember Level 59’s evidence: Freedmen’s Bureau schools, Hiram Revels in the Senate, Joseph Rainey in the House. Du Bois put people like them at the center of the story.

cards.headline: The verdict flips
cards.body: Building on the gains of the civil rights movement, revisionist scholars overturned the Dunning School’s picture. Eric Foner of Columbia University sums up the change: Reconstruction, long portrayed as a sordid time, has lately been viewed as a laudable experiment in interracial democracy. Same university as Dunning, opposite verdict.

cards.headline: Not a fairy tale either
cards.body: The newer view doesn’t claim Reconstruction was flawless. Southern Reconstruction governments offered lavish aid to railroads, and that program spawned corruption and rising taxes. The real difference is what gets blamed for its fall. The Dunning School blamed Black officeholders. The evidence of Level 59 points to Klan terror and the withdrawal of federal troops in 1877.

cards.headline: Reconstruction Remembered: explained
learned: The Dunning School called Reconstruction a mistake
Du Bois (1935) showed freedpeople shaping it
Revisionists see an experiment in interracial democracy
Real corruption doesn’t rescue the old verdict

questions.prompt: Which 1935 book showed that freedpeople actively shaped Reconstruction?

options.label: The Robber Barons, by Matthew Josephson
options.rationale: Josephson’s 1934 book was about Gilded Age tycoons (Level 64).

options.label: Black Reconstruction, by W. E. B. Du Bois
The Ideological Origins of the American Revolution, by Bernard Bailyn
options.rationale: Bailyn’s 1967 book was about the Revolution (Level 91).

options.label: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass

questions.explanation: W. E. B. Du Bois’s Black Reconstruction (1935) put freedpeople at the center of Reconstruction.

questions.prompt: A classmate says, “Newer historians admit there was corruption, so the Dunning School was right after all.” What is the best reply?

options.label: Admitting some corruption is not the same as calling the whole era a mistake
Newer historians deny there was any corruption
options.rationale: They say railroad aid spawned corruption.

options.label: The Dunning School praised Black officeholders
options.rationale: It blamed them for the South’s troubles.

options.label: Corruption proves the Klan ran Reconstruction
options.rationale: The Klan fought Reconstruction; it did not run it.

questions.explanation: Revisionists grant that railroad aid spawned corruption, but still see Reconstruction as a laudable experiment in interracial democracy, brought down by terror and the end of federal protection.

questions.prompt: Which evidence from Level 59 best fits Du Bois’s picture of freedpeople shaping Reconstruction?

options.label: Hayes withdrawing the last federal troops in 1877
options.rationale: That ended federal protection; it isn’t freedpeople acting.

options.label: The founding of the Klan in Pulaski, Tennessee
Hiram Revels and Joseph Rainey winning seats in Congress
Woodward’s theory of a secret bargain
options.rationale: That is a historian’s argument about 1877.

questions.explanation: Black men voted and won office: Revels became the first African American senator and Rainey the first African American in the House, both in 1870.
